findings: SCOPE: Read-only curation of commit 4f92a9742270a155f470aad5f06369bd76ed3092 and previously inspected/scored Balikci 2024 evidence, not independent/fresh biological or model validation. No repo files, original ledger or numerical JSON changed; no commits, PRs, pushes, contacts, agents, training, tuning or experiments. Downloads and derived arithmetic were kept outside the bare repository.

ESTIMAND: For each compound, R = reported mean catalytic IC50(NUDT14)/reported mean catalytic IC50(NUDT5), in matching µM units; L = log10(R) = log10(mean14) - log10(mean5). R>1/L>0 means the reported NUDT5 mean is lower; R<1/L<0 means the reported NUDT14 mean is lower. This is a ratio of reported means, not a mean of replicate ratios, mean log-ratio, intrinsic affinity ratio, confidence statement or binary selectivity class.

CENSORING CONTRACT: Two numeric positive means give a point R,L. Numeric numerator a with denominator >50 gives 0<R<a/50 and L<log10(a/50), strictly. Numerator >50 with numeric denominator d gives R>50/d and L>log10(50/d), strictly; no such lower-bound row occurs here. Both >50 allow any R>0/L real: no informative finite ratio bound or direction. Any target not tested makes the ratio unavailable, not inactive. Never replace >50 by 50, label double-censoring R=1, or treat a bound as a point.

IDENTITY CONTRACT: transfer.py identity() uses RDKit canonical isomeric SMILES for exact identity, FragmentParent then Uncharger for neutral_fragment_parent, and TautomerEnumerator.Canonicalize(neutral) for canonical_parent_tautomer. Exclude a source row if ANY of the three keys matches ANY training record, before paired-outcome analysis. InChIKey, compound name, scaffold and Tanimoto are not this exclusion rule. Parent/tautomer screening keys do not establish biological equivalence; tautomer handling can erase stereochemical detail. Keep original source structures unchanged.

ACTUAL EXCLUSIONS: Historical stored keys identify compound 10→ACT-20 and 11→ACT-19 on all three keys; 11 also equals candidate NC5-02, not another independent observation. No additional parent-only or tautomer-only overlaps occur. Stored source rows are unique under each of the three keys. Existing authenticated-reference sensitivity additionally makes compound 6 an ACT-01 overlap; both endpoints for 6 remain untested. Neither branch changes the paired nonoverlap cohort.

COUNTS: All 23 rows = 5 point-ratio rows (1,9,10,11,14), 1 strict upper-bound row (13), 0 lower-bound rows, 2 double-censored rows (12,15), 15 rows with an untested target (2,3,4,5,6,7,8,16,17a,17b,18a,18b,18c,19,N-Boc-protected 7). Historical nonoverlap total 21 = 3 points + 1 bound + 2 double-censored + 15 untested. Thus paired endpoint coverage n=6 (1,9,12,13,14,15), ratio-informative n=4, point-only n=3; these are compound counts, not paired raw replicate counts. Reference-sensitivity nonoverlap total 20 has the same six paired rows and 14 untested rows.

COUNT HAZARD: Existing measured_source_challenge.eligible_ids has 10 rows (1,2,3,4,5,9,12,13,14,15), because transfer.py parses only NUDT5 for eligibility. Rows 2,3,4,5 lack NUDT14 results and must not enter paired ratios. NUDT5 cell totals: 7 numeric/5 >50/11 untested; NUDT14: 6 numeric/2 >50/15 untested. Across targets: 13 numeric/7 censored/26 untested cells.

NONOVERLAP RATIOS: Compound 1: 0.990/0.837 = 1.182795698925, L=0.072909736604; 9: 0.162/0.270 = 0.600000000000, L=-0.221848749616; 14: 1.64/13.8 = 0.118840579710, L=-0.925035238354. Compound 13: 3.72/(>50) gives R<0.0744, L<-1.128427064454, not an exact ratio or confidence bound. Compounds 12 and 15: both >50, no informative finite R/L bound. Ratios/logs here are rounded only for display.

OVERLAP-ONLY DESCRIPTIVE RECORDS: 10 has R=0.263/0.487=0.540041067762, L=-0.267573212725; 11 has R=0.519/2.04=0.254411764706, L=-0.594462809577. Their historical Equal_mean scores 0.934919666574 and 0.922412275944 are training-overlap examples, not evidence from the six-row nonoverlap cohort; do not add them to inflate the sample or the high-score finding.

FROZEN SCORE CONTRACT: Join both raw endpoint strings and their separate status/mean/SD/censor fields to stored scores by unique source compound ID with exact source-SMILES/canonical-key consistency checks. Preserve the historical branch as primary and the existing reference_sensitivity branch separately; do not call score_panel(), measured_challenge(), reference_sensitivity() or run(), which fit/refit models. Retain all six existing score columns (RF, GBT, SVM_RBF, Nearest_active, Property_LR, Equal_mean). Equal_mean is the existing average of RF/GBT/SVM_RBF/Nearest_active, not of all six and not a calibrated target-selectivity probability.

ANSWER TO HIGH-SCORE QUESTION: Yes, descriptively. Within the six nonoverlap paired rows, compound 9 has the highest historical Equal_mean (0.811291844729), R=0.6, and submicromolar reported means for BOTH targets; compound 1 is second (0.684990188048), R≈1.183, also with both reported means <1 µM. The paper calls 9 a dual inhibitor. This shows high existing scores coexist with dual activity and a lower NUDT14 reported mean, not that the scores discriminate NUDT5 selectivity. Do not redefine dual using an invented cutoff or interpret numerical direction as statistically established preference.

ALL SIX HISTORICAL Equal_mean VALUES: In descending order, 9=0.811291844729; 1=0.684990188048; 14=0.325584813323; 12=0.254912305985; 13=0.253610946785; 15=0.236552724396. Stronger NUDT14-relative direction does not imply higher Equal_mean: 14 and upper-bounded 13 are lower-scoring. Methods differ: GBT is tied at 0.999974917535 for 1 and 9, while Property_LR for 14 is 0.928140823607. Report all methods instead of selecting the most favorable one.

PRESENTATION/INFERENCE CONTRACT: Use a per-compound score–ratio table or descriptive plot: points for 1,9,14; an open strict upper-bound marker/left arrow for 13 on an L axis; separate no-informative-ratio entries for 12,15; separate untested and overlap exclusions. Define high only through shown scores/ranks with the six-row denominator, not a tuned threshold. No selectivity labels, classification, ROC-AUC, threshold optimization, regression claim, p-value or reliable correlation conclusion from three points. Source/series exposure and close analogues remain after identity exclusion; nonoverlap is not an independent held-out discovery set.

UNCERTAINTY: Table 1 footnote a says IC50 values and SD derive from two independent biological replicates; Methods also says triplicate sets, while Figure 1 describes three technical replicates in a representative biological experiment. No raw paired IC50 replicates, cross-target covariance or ratio CI is supplied in the inspected table/CSV. SD is not CI or SEM. Do not calculate ratio/log error bars or significance by silently assuming independence, n=3/6, normality or paired observations; do not bootstrap three compounds into biological validation.

SOURCE AGREEMENT/DISAGREEMENT: All 16 Table 1 assay cells agree with author CSV and ledger; there is no paired-cohort numerical disagreement to hide. Outside this cohort, Figure 1B reports compound 4 as 13.9±0.6 versus CSV/ledger 13.9±0.62, and 5 as 21.2±1.0 versus 21.2±1.02 µM. Preserve both attributed SD representations; compatible rounding is an interpretation, not permission to rewrite either. Author CSV also has a trailing space in each of these two cells, removed in the ledger; the provenance phrase parsed cell values unchanged is not literally exact for whitespace.

SOURCE-VALUE SENSITIVITY: Primary paired values are Table 1 means, footnote censoring and author-CSV cross-checks. Carry caption-versus-CSV SD alternatives for 4/5 as separate source representations: means agree, NUDT14 is untested and neither row enters R, so this sensitivity changes no paired ratio, count or score join. Never invent a new paired discrepancy or impute missing NUDT14. More generally, retain conflicting source values with locations and analyze complete alternative source scenarios without averaging, choosing by score agreement or overwriting originals.

EXISTING SCORE SENSITIVITY ONLY: Read the already-stored authenticated ACT-01/ACT-02 graph-substitution results, do not rerun them or choose a preferred branch. Paired identities/R/L stay fixed. Reference-sensitivity Equal_mean in the same descending order is 9=0.829005171566; 1=0.703880723141; 14=0.408506680194; 12=0.343391265730; 13=0.340683085471; 15=0.318445788545. Ranking and the descriptive coexistence observation are unchanged; all methods and absolute changes should remain visible, not advertised as new robustness validation.

ASSAY/MISSINGNESS HAZARDS: Methods 4.3 uses recombinant catalytic AMP-Glo assays, 1 nM enzyme/10 µM ADPr, 1% DMSO, but NUDT5 incubation is 20 min and NUDT14 1 h. The shared 500 nM TH5427=0%-activity normalizer has no stated NUDT14 exception, despite the paper describing TH5427 as NUDT5-selective and the CSV marking compound 6 untested for IC50 on both targets. Control use is not a titration; retain those missing IC50s. This unresolved normalization concern limits interpreting R as intrinsic selectivity; it is not proof of failure, and cannot be repaired by silently changing controls or dropping compound 6 from an already compound-6-free paired panel.

SCOPE/PROVENANCE HAZARDS: The Results phrase all compounds were tested occurs in Table 1 SAR context; it cannot override 26 explicit untested cells across the 23-row CSV. SPR KD, NanoBRET EC50, CETSA or cell viability do not fill catalytic IC50s. The stored transfer manifest records historical git_revision 8c2a1b6990df1e140e15ab5a0eabea69b70eee14 with git_dirty=true, not a run at pinned commit 4f92a974; all ten recorded input hashes nevertheless match pinned blobs. Preserve this history and do not claim a new reproduction.

VERIFICATION LIMIT: Verified source transcription, byte integrity, stored identity-key equality/joins, counts and ratio/log arithmetic only. RDKit identity functions were read, not rerun; stored matches were checked against stored historical/replacement identities. No new model scores, biochemical experiments, model-validation tests, repo tests, lint or build were run for this read-only curation.
